title: Open Problem: PTAS for weighted minimization problems in fractionally treewidth-fragile classes
statement_text: For the minimization problems, we do not know whether fractional treewidth-fragility is sufficient even for the distance-1 problems. In particular, consider the Minimum Vertex Cover problem in fractionally treewidth-fragile graphs, or more generally in hereditary classes with sublinear separators: while the unweighted version can be dealt with by the local search method, we do not know whether there exists a PTAS for the weighted version of this problem.
context_text: A PTAS is an algorithm that, for each fixed $k$, returns in polynomial time a solution within a factor $1\pm1/k$ of the optimum. A set $S$ is a balanced separator of $G$ if every component of $G\setminus S$ has at most $|V(G)|/2$ vertices; a hereditary class has sublinear separators if, for some $c<1$, every graph in it has a balanced separator of size $O(|V(G)|^c)$ (e.g. planar graphs, proper minor-closed classes, many geometric classes). A class $\mathcal{G}$ is efficiently fractionally treewidth-fragile if there are a function $f$ and a polynomial-time algorithm that, given $k$ and $G\in\mathcal{G}$, returns sets $X_1,\dots,X_m\subseteq V(G)$ such that each vertex lies in at most $m/k$ of them, together with tree decompositions of each $G\setminus X_i$ of width at most $f(k)$; this holds for proper minor-closed classes, classes with sublinear separators and bounded maximum degree, and many geometric classes, and Dvořák conjectured that every hereditary class with sublinear separators is fractionally treewidth-fragile. Distance-1 problems are those where admissibility of a vertex set depends only on adjacencies (like independent set or vertex cover), while distance-$r$ problems involve dependencies over distance $r$. The paper's main result gives a PTAS, in every efficiently fractionally treewidth-fragile class, for all maximization problems on vertex-weighted graphs that are determined by distances at most $r$, (near-)monotone (subsets of admissible sets remain admissible, up to a bounded correction) and solvable in polynomial time on bounded treewidth (e.g. weighted maximum $r$-independent set), and a QPTAS for them in all hereditary classes with sublinear separators. Minimization problems such as Minimum Vertex Cover are not monotone in this sense; unweighted Minimum Vertex Cover has a PTAS in classes with sublinear separators by local search (Har-Peled and Quanrud), but the weighted case is open.
